title: 2026 Ligand Recognition and Molecular Gating Gordon Research Conference and Gordon Research Seminar
text:
Channels, transporters and G-protein coupled receptors are important classes of membrane proteins that
play key roles in human physiology and are major pharmaceutical targets, as their dysfunctions cause
neurological, muscular, cardiovascular, endocrine and metabolic diseases. At this conference, the latest
scientific progress aimed at resolving their structure and functional mechanism in an integrated context of
membrane lipid and protein environment will be presented and discussed.

title: Leading Edge Propogation Mechanism of Human Keloid Scars
text:
Keloids are skin scarring disorders that exhibit continuous tissue growth and are only found in humans. The
proposed work will combine mathematical modeling, gene expression analysis, and functional tests in
human-on-mouse skin transplantation model to discover molecules that sustain continuous expansion of keloid
scars. The results of this study will inform new understanding of human keloid scarring and other continuously
expanding skin diseases.

title: Rifaximin as a Therapeutic Agent for Reducing Endotoxemia and Fibrosis in Neonatal Cholestasis
text:
Biliary atresia (BA) is a neonatal cholestatic liver disease which is the leading cause of pediatric liver
transplants. Preventing inflammation-mediated progression of fibrosis activated by gut-derived endotoxin may
be a potential treatment to reduce the incidence of liver transplantation in BA. We aim to test this hypothesis by
treating bile duct ligated neonatal piglets with a safe, clinically available, non-absorbable antibiotic and
examine immune activation and fibrosis development.

title: Digital Assessment of Motor Skills in Infants and young boys with Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy using Wearable Sensors
text:
Wearable sensors can provide objective and reliable signatures of motor abilities including important real-world
functional adaptations which cannot be reliably evaluated during in-clinic assessments. Sensor-derived
biomarkers can facilitate infants and toddlers with Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy (DMD) to be treated with FDA-
approved medications and for inclusion in future clinical trials of novel therapies.

title: Exploring the Novel Functions of Cyclin Ds in T Cells and Tumor Progression
text:
Limited T-cell tumor trafficking and survival are two major challenges in treating solid tumors with adoptive T-cell
therapy. This study will define the unknown intrinsic mechanisms in downregulating T-cell solid tumor infiltration
and survival mediated through the kinase-independent functions of cell cycle proteins. We are developing a new
approach, representing a dramatic shift in immunotherapy, to break the barrier of T-cell therapy for patients with
solid tumors by manipulating the expression of cell cycle proteins in T cells.

title: Develop an AI-Powered Digital Platform for Remote Oral Disease Detection and Prediction
text:
Oral diseases remain a widespread and preventable public health burden, with most diagnoses occurring only
after conditions have progressed beyond reversible stages. SMARTeeth++ is an innovative, AI-powered
bioengineering platform that extends diagnostic and predictive capabilities beyond traditional dental clinics by
integrating portable imaging, machine learning-based detection, and big-data modeling.
 This system has the potential to transform oral healthcare delivery from a reactive, treatment-focused
model to a proactive, prevention-oriented approach, aligned with NIDCR’s priority to accelerate adoption of
reliable and scalable diagnostic tools.

title: Respiration and Generalized Epilepsies
text:
Generalized seizures are brain-wide events and occur in several types of epilepsy. Asking a
patient to hyperventilate is a reliable strategy to diagnose generalized absence seizures – rapid
breathing triggers a seizure in nearly 100% of patients. Identifying the biological processes that
intimately link respiration and generalized seizures will lead to a better understanding of how the
brain triggers seizures and will pave the way forward in developing better treatments.

title: Molecular mechanism in noise-induced hearing loss
text:
Currently, no established pharmacological treatments for the prevention and management of noise-induced
hearing loss (NIHL) exist, owing largely to the lack of a comprehensive understanding of the precise molecular
mechanisms and signaling pathways mediating sensory hair cell injury. This resubmission of a competing
renewal application employs preclinical mouse models subjected to a variety of severities of noise exposure for
investigation of both molecular mechanisms and prevention of NIHL by applying cutting-edge analytical
technology. The outcome of this proposal will guide the design of novel clinical interventions for the prevention
of NIHL, benefiting the quality of life of individuals and reducing healthcare costs.

title: Visual Play: An Interactive Play Idea and AAC Grid Generator to Assist in Behavioral Interventions for Minimally Verbal Autistic Children
text:
Autism is an increasingly prevalent neurodevelopmental disorder that often causes severe speech and
language impairments. Talking tappable grids of words can help autistic children learn to talk when used during
speech and behavioral therapy, but they are hard to program and use during play sessions. We propose a new
app that automates much of the work required, so this critical technology can be used by therapists working
with autistic children during a period in their life where a transition to speech is most possible.

title: Small molecule inhibitors of hyperphosphorylated tau aggregation in Alzheimer's disease: lead optimization, and proof of concept in a rodent model
text:
The distribution of aggregated hyperphosphorylated tau (p-tau) in the brain correlates well with cognitive
impairments observed in different stages of Alzheimer’s disease (AD). AD is currently untreatable, and the
mechanisms underlying p-tau aggregation in AD are not fully understood. The proposed research plan will
propel small molecule therapeutics that curtail human p-tau aggregation (isoform 1N4R) through lead
optimization and proof of concept studies to improve our understanding of the mechanisms underlying AD
and tauopathies.

title: Cutaneous opioid circuitry in skin inflammation and sensation
text:
Endogenous opioid peptides regulate the cutaneous sensations of itch and pain and have critical homeostatic
functions. My preliminary work implicates a role of opioid enkephalin circuit in regulating skin sensory and
inflammatory function. In this proposal, I aim to define the precise mechanisms by which enkephalin
regulates cutaneous inflammation and noxious sensation, with the ultimate goal of identifying therapeutic
strategies for chronic inflammatory skin disease management.

title: MATCHMAKERS: SOLVING TCR RECOGNITION AND DESIGN VIA INTEGRATED HIGH-THROUGHPUT SCREENING, STRUCTURAL, FUNCTIONAL, AND COMPUTATIONAL APPROACHES
text: Understanding how T cell receptors (TCRs) see tumor antigens presented by MHCs is necessary to fully understand how the immune system recognizes tumor antigens, and to reap the full potential of antigen-specific immunotherapy. To achieve this goal, a quantum leap forward is required in which the revolutionary advances in machine learning are combined with a large volume of structure, function, data on matched TCR-pMHC pairs. The development of accurate predictors of TCR-antigen recognition will be dependent on the creation and integration sequencing-based datasets with high-throughput structural and functional insights. Our proposal, submitted as a CRUK/NCI Grand Challenge team (MATCHMAKERS) will combine researchers with expertise in immunology, methods development, structural biology, and computation to enable generalized prediction and design of TCR recognition. This work will be spread across four Work Packages (WPs): WP1: Large-scale generation of TCR-pMHC pairs from naturally occurring sources. We will build datasets of naturally occurring TCR-pMHC pairs. Our team will use an array of approaches to collect these datasets, from humans and from mouse models, and in the context of both cancer and immunity more generally. WP2: Ultra-high throughput TCR-pMHC matching using molecular engineering. Efforts to create general models will require a broader array of data than feasible to collect from natural TCR systems. We will use an array of synthetic approaches developed by our team to comprehensively match TCRs with pMHCs to train computational models. WP3: Large-scale structural and biochemical analyses of TCR-pMHC interactions. A key to our team’s vision is to match interaction datasets with high throughput structural and functional insights. A deep understanding of how the TCR contacts with MHC helices control function and orientation will be essential for training and testing computational models. WP4 AI-based prediction and design of TCR-pMHC interactions. We will integrate our data to train next- generation algorithms capable of generally predicting and designing TCR-pMHC interactions. These predictions will proceed through a reiterative testing and feedback circuits for further model optimization.

title: Determining how neurotensin mediates valence processing and compulsive cocaine seeking
text:
This project aims to explore how neuromodulation, specifically neurotensin, plays a critical role in valence
assignment in the basolateral amygdala, a site identified as a divergence point in circuits mediating positive
and negative valence. This project will test the hypotheses that neurotensin directs valence-specific information
to the appropriate downstream BLA projections during valence processing and modulates compulsive cocaine-
seeking behavior. The proposed research project will broaden our understanding of the fundamental
neuromodulatory mechanisms underlying valence processing and motivated behavior and identify neurotensin
as a novel target for treating valence-disorders including substance use disorders.

title: Epigenetic mechanisms of adaptive plasticity in glioblastoma
text:
Brain tumors such as glioblastoma are relentlessly malignant and resistant to therapeutic intervention,
possibly due to a concept known as adaptive plasticity whereby tumor cells are able to change their
dependencies and vulnerabilities to survive. This proposal aims to use complex models of glioblastoma to
determine how adaptive plasticity affects treatment resistance, and determine if there are ways to predict
how cells will change during therapy to better target them. In addition, we will determine if targeting the
underlying epigenetic processes that allow for adaptive plasticity is a viable therapeutic strategy for
preventing tumor cell escape. This work will provide novel therapeutic strategies to prevent tumor recurrence
after therapy in glioblastoma.

title: The Evolution of Gene Regulation and Human Disease
text:
Given a person’s genome sequence, it remains challenging to make accurate and unbiased predictions about
their risk for most diseases. We are developing computational methods that integrate recent advances in ma-
chine learning, the wealth of available genomic data, and evolutionary perspectives to predict how any individ-
ual’s unique combination of genetic variants influences the control of genes. These methods will enable identi-
fication of new disease mechanisms and more accurate estimation of genetic risk for common diseases.

title: Dynamics of the cellular and molecular architecture of human pulmonary TB granulomas
text:
RELEVANCE TO PUBLIC HEALTH
Granulomas are collections of macrophages and lymphocytes that characterize a range of chronic
inflammatory conditions. Here, we will investigate the cellular and molecular architecture of human tuberculosis
granulomas to learn about how these structures mediate antimicrobial activity against the intracellular
bacterium that causes tuberculosis as well as contribute to disease pathogenesis. The insights gained from
this study are critical for understanding protective immunity against tuberculosis towards developing new
strategies for prevention and treatment.

title: The Sleep and Dementia Consortium: a harmonized resource for studying the contributions of poor sleep to Incident Alzheimer's disease and related dementia
text:
Although sleep of sufficient quality and durations is associated with optimal brain health, the role
of poor sleep in the development of Alzheimer’s disease and related dementias (ADRD) remains
equivocal. We propose to address this by extending the Sleep and Dementia Consortium
(SDC); the largest and most comprehensive group of community-based cohort studies
dedicated to understanding the contributions of poor sleep to ADRD. Through rigorous analysis
of up to 10,684 participants with gold-standard polysomnographic sleep assessments across 7
studies, we will investigate the complexities of sleep-ADRD associations to determine if the
screening, management, and treatment of poor sleep may have benefits for protecting against
dementia.

title: Development of Two Novel AMD Models for Evaluation of RPE Protection by the Novel Antioxidant D-DHA
text:
The proposed work on the development of two new mouse models of age-related macular
degeneration (AMD) and testing a new potential therapy (oral D-DHA) is important for protecting
human health because AMD can cause loss of central vision. Current treatments are limited,
especially for the advanced dry (geographic atrophy) form of the disease. If these mouse
models are protected by D-DHA, this will also implicate DHA oxidation as a key pathogenic
mechanism in the models.

title: Dysfunctional organelle-specific autophagy leads to brain ischemia-reperfusion injury
text:
Transient cerebral ischemia occurs in many clinical settings, including transient ischemic
attack, cardiac arrest, hypovolemic shock, etc. Most cerebral ischemia survivors have long-term neurological
sequelae due to brain ischemia reperfusion injury. This proposal will use state-of-the-art animal models and
advanced imaging technologies to study the underlying mechanisms and corresponding treatment strategies for
brain ischemia reperfusion injury.

title: Low-voltage liquid lens enabled endoscopic optical coherence tomography
text:
A current challenge for cardiologists is the ability to generate high resolution images of the heart. This is driven
by the lack of compact forward-viewing endoscopic micro-optical coherence tomography systems. In the
proposed research, we will develop an innovative compact endoscope containing a low-voltage electrowetting
adaptive element with an ultimate goal of forward-viewing endoscopic micro-optical coherence tomography in a
surgical setting.
